old_problem: The active review requested approval but did not state that the source itself omits a marker-removal step before AC recovery. With an immediate-shutdown policy, leaving a persistent marker or latch is a material recovery hazard, and neither public standards nor the source define how to clear it after host loss.
disposition_reason: Caution3 is a private OEM fault injection whose 106 C mapping, 'immediate' timing, shutdown-versus-power-cut behavior and cleanup cannot be inferred from Linux/IPMI/Redfish. ED-03 prohibits guessing OEM semantics; ED-06/ED-18 require explicit shutdown and AC phases; ED-09 makes physical power work manual; ED-16 requires an approved injection and recovery; ED-17 requires persistent evidence. The missing post-shutdown marker/latch-clear method is core safety recovery, so this case cannot be review-resolved without Wistron authority.
decision_basis: Directly read Compatibility row415 all 18 XLSX columns, same-row DeepSeek material, GPT V2/history3007 and adjacent caution2 row414 plus dmesg row416.
Distinguished caution3's immediate 106 C shutdown from caution2's delayed 104 C policy and caution1's alert/fan-only response.
Identified that host logs alone cannot establish the event-to-power-loss interval; externally persistent BMC/power evidence is mandatory.
Identified the source's absent marker-removal step as an unresolved recovery hazard before AC-on, rather than silently inventing a cleanup method.
Directly read next formal queue Compatibility row416 and verified its manifest identity; no marker, shutdown, AC cycle or DUT/BMC action ran.

test_case.test_name: OEM-approved caution3 synthetic 106 C immediate shutdown and cold recovery
test_case.purpose: Inject the exact approved caution3 condition and prove the target firmware records the 106 C critical state, performs its specified immediate protective shutdown, then recovers without a latched injection after controlled cleanup and AC cycling.
required_package: Wistron-controlled caution3 specification for exact BMC/controller, firmware, marker path and injection/latch semantics
Approved 106 C sensor/value tolerance, critical event IDs, definition/tolerance of immediate, and shutdown-versus-hard-power-cut signature
Qualified BMC/power operator, drained maintenance window and external timestamped BMC/rail/LED recorder
Vendor-approved marker/latch removal while host is down, AC OFF/ON method and POST/OS/eight-GPU/BMC recovery oracle
test_case.test_command: PENDING OEM AUTHORITY. After workload drain, baseline and preserve SDR/SEL/dmesg/power evidence and start an external recorder. A qualified operator creates the exact approved caution3 marker once at the specified BMC console. Correlate the mapped 106 C state, critical event and external power transition against the signed immediate-time tolerance. Before any AC-on action, use the approved out-of-band method to prove the marker and associated latch are cleared; then perform one separately authorized AC OFF-to-ON sequence and verify POST, OS Ready, all GPUs and BMC health.
test_case.expected_result: The intended synthetic sensor alone reports 106 C and generates the exact critical event, followed by the specified protective shutdown within the approved immediate interval and with the correct power signature. Cleanup is proven before AC-on; one cold recovery reaches POST, OS Ready, complete GPU enumeration and healthy BMC state without a shutdown loop or residual fault.
test_case.pass_fail_basis: PENDING: PASS is forbidden until OEM authority defines marker/latch behavior, sensor/event oracle, immediate timing and power signature, cleanup and cold recovery. After approval, every phase must have externally persistent evidence; a marker readback, critical log or successful power-on by itself cannot pass.
safety_gate: Prove caution3 is supported and non-heating on the exact firmware; approve intentional immediate shutdown and data-loss impact
Drain workloads/filesystems, preserve SEL/dmesg and log sensor/event/power outside the host
Provide independent management, qualified BMC/power operator and a verified marker/latch-clear method before AC-on
Stop on wrong sensor/event/timing/power state, real thermal anomaly, cleanup uncertainty or access loss; never auto-retry or repeat the AC cycle
expected_evidence: Signed caution3/controller/firmware, timing, power and recovery specification
Marker action, 106 C SDR identity, complete critical event and synchronized external power/LED timeline
Measured event-to-shutdown interval and shutdown-versus-power-cut signature
Marker/latch absence before AC-on plus one authorized OFF/ON record
POST, OS Ready, all-GPU/BMC post-health and operator/engineer verdict
test_case.recovery: Do not apply AC until the OEM-approved out-of-band procedure proves the marker and any thermal-policy latch clear. If that proof or the shutdown signature is unavailable, preserve evidence and escalate without cycling. After one authorized cold recovery, stop on any repeated shutdown or missing device and never clear SEL or retry automatically.
